It adds the required replayable multipart convenience API while preserving and reusing FilesService.Add. Candidate B changes Add’s behavior and bypasses it from Upload, directly contradicting two explicit requirements.","reasons":["A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and passes its buffered body and content type through s.Add, exactly following the established path required by the contract.","A preserves FilesService.Add unchanged, retaining its validation, option handling, request construction, response decoding, and existing error semantics.","A validates empty fileName and nil content before invoking multipart construction or making a request.","B changes Add to eagerly consume and buffer every custom multipart body. This alters behavior, memory use, error timing, and error text despite the explicit requirement to preserve Add’s existing behavior and avoid retry-machinery changes around it consistency-wise (it also introduces a private alternate path). Changelog’s claim that Add is now replayable reflects this out-of-scope semantic expansion, not a contract win here given frozen instructions trump task prose ambiguity. Most critically frozen explicitly says preserve Add behavior lower-level custom multipart API, and route Upload through existing Add method. Candidate A does so. Candidate B does not: Upload calls private add directly, duplicating/bypassing public Add validation/buffering semantics and making future behavior divergence more likely. Test quality: B stronger multipart retry verification with os.File and verifies every attempt; A only counts attempts and uses strings.NewReader, and no validation/error reader tests. Candidate A tests multipart field/name/content separately and retries but weak streamed simulation. Neither tests validation/source-reader failures visible. Candidate B's extra Add retry test validates behavior forbidden by contract. Winner A despite test gaps."],"risks_a":["The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than an os.File or deliberately non-replayable streaming reader, so it weakly represents the reported streamed-content case.","The retry handler does not verify multipart field, filename, and content on both attempts; an empty or corrupted replay could still receive a successful response.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, despite the contract explicitly requesting them."],"risks_b":["It changes Add from pass-through behavior to eager in-memory buffering, violating the requirement to preserve Add’s existing behavior and potentially affecting large custom bodies, blocking behavior, and error semantics.","Upload calls the new private add helper instead of FilesService.Add, violating the explicit reuse requirement and creating duplicate routing machinery.","It wraps Add source-read errors with new text, changing established error semantics further beyond scope; it also moves option construction until after full reader consumption and applies no direct Upload validation in visible code (relying on multipartbody.NewFile internals). No visible tests cover required validation or source-reader error propagation."]}
